paper.title: Safe Task Planning with Long-Term Graph Memory for Embodied Agents

read: full text (arXiv HTML): Sections 1-6 and Appendices A (method details), B (simulated and real-world settings, hyperparameters, token cost); prompt listings skimmed

claims.claim: A vision-language task planner for household robots that sees only through its own camera can avoid safety hazards it saw earlier but can no longer see (a power strip, a flammable box, a contaminant) if it keeps a persistent scene graph of objects and their spatial relations built from its RGB-D views, and a separate model checks each planned action against that graph and forces a replan when it predicts a hazard. Supported only if, on IS-Bench tasks converted to single egocentric RGB-D views where the hazard is seen and then occluded, its safe-success rate (task done and safety goal met) is at least 35 points higher on average than each prompt-based safe-planning baseline and than the same system without the graph, with task success no more than 5 points below the best baseline; and if on a physical arm, over 10 trials on each of four hazard tasks, it succeeds safely in at least 90% of trials per task while every baseline does so in at most 30%.
claims.decision_rule: Partial-observability avg SSR >= +0.35 over SaP, CoT, Base and w/o GM; avg SR within 0.05 of best baseline; real Franka SSR >= 0.9 on all 4 tasks with all baselines <= 0.3.

claims.claim: For safety-aware planning under partial observability, how past observations are remembered matters more than whether they are remembered: a structured relational memory of objects (what is in, on or near what), with unseen objects kept rather than deleted and relations updated after each action, preserves safety much better than storing all past images, retrieving past observations by similarity, or keeping a flat list of seen objects. Supported only if, with the same planner and risk checker, the graph memory's safe-success rate is at least 20 points higher than each of those three alternatives, and if removing either object retention or relation updating lowers safe success by at least 20 points.
claims.decision_rule: Graph SSR >= +0.20 over full-history, RAG and object-list memory; w/o retention and w/o edge update each >= 0.20 below full.

experiments.text: Build the memory and planning loop. Setup: at each step Gemini 2.5 Flash lists objects in the egocentric RGB-D view and SAM 2 segments them; nodes carry masks and depth-based 3D positions, edges carry IN / ON / NEAR relations proposed by the language model and refined geometrically from depth. Across steps nodes are matched by mask IoU with bipartite matching; objects that leave the view are retained, and edges are updated when an action moves an object. A GPT-4o risk predictor reads the graph, the task and the next planned action, estimates whether a hazard will arise and, above a conservatism threshold eta = 0.8, sends a replan signal with an explanation to a GPT-4o planner that picks actions from a fixed skill set.

Turn the benchmark into a partial-observability test. Setup: IS-Bench in OmniGibson, 17 tasks over four hazard categories (3 electric shock, 2 fire, 6 falling, 6 food contamination, preserving the benchmark's imbalance), task and safety goals given as BDDL predicates on fixed pre-sampled scenes; the original top-down plus four fixed cameras are replaced by one egocentric 1280x720 RGB-D camera, so the hazard is seen early and then occluded during execution. Success rate (SR) counts task goals met; safe success rate (SSR) requires both task and safety goals. Baselines with the same GPT-4o planner and skill set: SaP (a learned safety cognition prompt), the benchmark's safety chain-of-thought prompt, the plain planner, and the method without graph memory (risk predictor on raw observations).

Compare under partial observability. Result: average SR / SSR 0.79 / 0.59 against 0.79 / 0.13 for SaP, 0.83 / 0.17 for chain-of-thought, 0.59 / 0.00 for the plain planner and 0.75 / 0.21 without graph memory. Per hazard, SSR is 0.67 / 0.50 / 0.67 / 0.50 (electric, fire, falling, food) against at most 0.33 / 0.00 / 0.33 / 0.17 for any baseline; fire tasks remain hard for all methods (SR 0.50).

Deploy on a physical arm. Setup: Franka Panda with a RealSense D405 egocentric RGB-D camera on a tabletop, one task per hazard category (watering a plant with a power strip nearby, moving a handkerchief with an object on it, heating vegetables beside a cardboard box, putting an apple in a basket beside bleach), 10 trials each with small layout changes, same GPT-4o planner and risk predictor. Result: SR is 0.6-1.0 for every method, but SSR is 1.0 on all four tasks for the full system against 0.0-0.1 for SaP, chain-of-thought and the plain planner and 0.3 / 0.0 / 0.0 / 0.0 without graph memory.

Check full observability, where memory should matter less. Setup: original IS-Bench camera layout plus depth, so the hazard stays visible. Result: average SR / SSR 0.88 / 0.67 against 0.92 / 0.42 without graph memory, 0.88 / 0.21 for chain-of-thought, 0.79 / 0.21 for the plain planner and 0.88 / 0.13 for SaP; the risk predictor alone already beats the prompt-based methods, and the graph adds 25 points on top.

Check that the risk predictor does not hurt hazard-free tasks. Setup: run the tasks with hazards removed. Result: average SR 0.82 against 0.76 for the plain planner and 0.88 for chain-of-thought, so the replan signal rarely fires unnecessarily.

Swap the memory representation. Setup: partial observability, same planner and risk predictor, replacing the graph with the full history of images, retrieval of past observations by similarity (RAG), or a flat list of observed objects. Result: SR / SSR 0.79 / 0.59 for the graph, 0.58 / 0.13 for full history, 0.79 / 0.38 for RAG and 0.88 / 0.17 for the object list; the object list keeps task success highest but loses the spatial relations that define most hazards.

Remove the graph's update rules. Setup: delete nodes that leave the view instead of retaining them, or freeze edges instead of updating them after actions. Result: SR / SSR 0.71 / 0.21 without retention and 0.71 / 0.38 without edge updates, against 0.79 / 0.59 for the full graph.

Check sensitivity to the replan threshold and the cost. Setup: conservatism factor eta 0.8 versus 1, and per-step tokens and latency. Result: at eta = 1 safety violations drop from 6/17 to 3/17 and SSR rises from 0.59 to 0.67 with SR unchanged at 0.79, so the headline setting is not the most favourable one; per planning step the full system uses 9,425 tokens and 17.6 s against 3,980 tokens and 10.3 s for the plain planner and 6,101 tokens and 12.4 s without graph memory.

dropped: Prompt listings; graph-construction visualisations. Stated limitation (hazards must appear in past or current views) kept implicit in c0's setup.
notes: Drafted from scratch from arXiv HTML for the dataset50 rebuild, without consulting earlier claims or references. c0 SR bar: 0.79 vs best 0.83 (CoT) = 4 points. Real-world 'every baseline at most 30%' is set by w/o GM electric 0.3.
